summary: this is the object a method or constructor is running on. You need this.name when a parameter has the same name as the field, so Java can tell the two apart.
notes: In BrokenStudent, name = name; assigns the parameter to itself. The field stays null and the numbers stay 0.
this.name = name; copies the parameter into the field.
setGpa(double gpa) uses this.gpa for the same reason.
pitfall: Writing name = name; compiles with no error, so the bug only shows up later as null or 0 when you print the field.
